title: Localization in microcavities revealed by phase-space non-Hermitian skin effect
authors: Jung-Wan Ryu, Yong-Hoon Lee, Muhan Choi, Chang-Hwan Yi, Martina Hentschel
abstract: Contrary to the semiclassical expectation for fully chaotic systems, localization of resonances is found to be a common feature in open microcavities. In spiral-shaped dielectric microcavities, a substantial fraction of resonances localize on polygonal patterns in real space, are chiral, and their momentum distributions accumulate near the critical line for total internal reflection. Despite the extensive investigation, the physical mechanism responsible for their remarkable abundance has remained a long-standing question. Addressing this, we reveal a physical correspondence between an inhomogeneous-loss Hatano-Nelson model and the dielectric phase space of a spiral microcavity. We show that the combination of geometry-induced momentum drift and refractive escape yields a generalized non-Hermitian skin effect in the phase space momentum. We identify this mechanism as the origin of the critical-line localization of resonances in open chaotic spiral microcavities, extending the skin-effect concept beyond nonreciprocal lattices to phase space and to open chaotic wave systems.
summary: This paper reveals that the unexpected localization of resonances in open spiral microcavities is caused by a generalized non-Hermitian skin effect acting in the phase space momentum. The authors map the physical geometry to an inhomogeneous-loss Hatano-Nelson model, showing that the combination of geometric momentum drift and refractive escape drives this critical-line localization.
main_problem: The paper addresses the physical mechanism responsible for the systematic accumulation of localized resonances near the critical line for total internal reflection in open, chaotic spiral microcavities.
main_result: The localization is attributed to a generalized non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE) occurring in the phase space momentum, extending the concept beyond standard nonreciprocal lattices.
method: The authors establish a physical correspondence between the microcavity's dielectric phase space and an inhomogeneous-loss Hatano-Nelson model, analyzing the resulting spectral and spatial properties.
model_or_system: The system is an open, spiral-shaped dielectric microcavity. The dynamics are mapped onto an inhomogeneous-loss Hatano-Nelson model, incorporating geometry-induced momentum drift and refractive escape governed by a critical momentum $p_c$.
key_observables: Localized resonances, momentum distributions accumulating near $p_c$, complex-energy spectrum, and Boundary Husimi distribution $H(s, p)$.
important_parameters: Critical momentum $p_c = 1/n$, hopping asymmetry ratio $t_R / t_L$, and the degree of loss ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a physical correspondence between the dielectric dynamics and the Hatano-Nelson model, and that the dominant localization peak can be reliably identified via $p_{	ext{max}}$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate localized resonances in the microcavity vs. closed billiard, the Hatano-Nelson model spectrum showing separation, and the Poincaré surface of section detailing momentum drift and the role of $p_c$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the localization anomaly, establishing the mapping to the Hatano-Nelson model, demonstrating the generalized NHSE mechanism via momentum drift and escape, and finally confirming this mechanism using detailed phase-space diagnostics.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, generalized framework for understanding localization in open, wave-guiding structures by connecting geometric optics (TIR) to the mathematical formalism of non-Hermitian physics (NHSE).
